title: the db client finds its passfile when a proof repoints the instance root
intention: store._conn_args() returns a passfile that exists whenever the startup instance root holds one, even if a proof has repointed ROOTS['instance'] at a scratch dir.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: test_charter_held.py tooth test_the_backpack_receives_and_reads_back_feedback fails on akiendell with OperationalError: connection to server at 127.0.0.1, port 5432 failed: fe_sendauth: no password supplied; the proof sets address.ROOTS['instance'] to a scratch dir and store._conn_args() takes passfile from instance_path('db_domain', 0)
traces_to: Law 3: the proof world must be able to reach the one door to 5432 the same way on every box; Law 4: found by the client, not by each proof remembering to copy a credential.
how: In cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py, when instance_path('db_domain', 0)/pgpass is absent, fall back to the pgpass under the instance root the process started with (address's startup root); an existing file under the current root still wins. Red-first proof repoints ROOTS['instance'] at an empty temp dir and asserts the passfile names an existing file.

clauses.claim: with ROOTS['instance'] repointed at an empty scratch dir and no unix socket, _conn_args()['passfile'] names a file that exists, where it named a missing one before
with ROOTS['instance'] untouched, _conn_args()['passfile'] is still instance_path('db_domain', 0)/pgpass

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.
the proof roots its import at the checkout: REPO = parents[6] (parents[5] is cairn/)

orient.request: fc4bb2062253: the db client finds its passfile when a proof repoints the instance root (cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py)
orient.intent: store._conn_args() falls back to the pgpass under the box's own instance root when the current (repointed) root holds none, so a proof that repoints ROOTS['instance'] still reaches 5432 over TCP on a box with no unix socket.
orient.scope: store._conn_args and one new proof beside the client's test_client.py; no other db_domain code, no proof that repoints the root is edited
unknowns: the fallback is the box default Path.home()/.cairn, not a per-process captured root, so a process launched with a different HOME and a repointed root reads that HOME's pgpass
